_hinweis: Content for /syllabus (src/pages/kursinhalte.astro, src/pages/kursinhalte/[level].astro, src/components/KursProgression.astro) and the lesson-plan generator (src/lib/stundenplan.js, which links each grammar line to a topic page by the patterns in GRAMMAR_RULES, so keep the wording of a grammar line close to the topic's name). Everything here is our own, written from the CEFR can-do descriptors. Never copy from coursebooks, from the exam bodies' syllabi or from any official question bank: no unit titles, no tables of contents, no texts. `lehrwerke` would name coursebook series only ("goes with"), without a level after the name; the lists are empty until Edgar decides whether to name any (scripts/check-lehrwerk-leak.mjs fails the build on series + level). To add a level: insert an object in `niveaus` (order = order on the page and in the timeline); the id becomes the URL (/syllabus/<id>). `pruefung` from A2.2 (CILS, CELI, PLIDA, CERT.IT; see docs/content-plan.md §2): name the exam and the skill, never a task number, a timing or a word count, because those facts are unverified until the exam items check them. `selbstcheck`: exactly 5 sentences describing what a learner can do BEFORE this level.

probestunde._hinweis: Empty = no trial-lesson button (there is no booking page yet). Once there is one, put its path here, e.g. "/probestunde". {niveau} is replaced by the level.

niveaus.label: A1.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about yourself, your family and your day, in simple sentences.

kannZiele: You can introduce yourself: name, country, languages.
You can ask other people their name and where they are from.
You can spell your name.
grammatik: Subject pronouns: io, tu, Lei, noi, voi
essere and stare: sono, sei, è; sto bene
Question words: come, chi, dove, di dove
wortschatz: The alphabet and spelling your name

kannZiele: You can say your phone number, address and age.
You can fill in a simple form.
grammatik: Numbers up to 1,000: uno, ventuno, cento
Yes/no questions and negation with non
essere and avere: sono di…, ho trent'anni
wortschatz: Forms: nome, cognome, indirizzo, data di nascita

kannZiele: You can introduce your family.
You can say who belongs to you and how old they are.
grammatik: Possessives: mio, tuo, suo (il mio libro, mia madre)
Nouns and gender: il fratello, la sorella
Plurals: figli, genitori, amici

kannZiele: You can describe your flat and your furniture.
You can say what is in your home and where it is.
grammatik: Articles: il, lo, la, l', un, uno, una
c'è / ci sono: C'è un divano. Il divano è qui.
Adjectives: agreement (la cucina piccola)

kannZiele: You can ask for products and prices in a shop.
You can order in a bar.
You can write a shopping list.
grammatik: Articles: i, gli, le (i pomodori, gli spinaci)
Polite requests: Vorrei…, Mi dà…?
Demonstratives: questo, quello
Question words: quanto costa?
wortschatz: Containers (una bottiglia di, un pacco di)

kannZiele: You can describe your daily routine with times.
You can say how often you do something.
grammatik: Present tense: regular -are, -ere, -ire verbs (also finire, capire)
Telling the time: alle otto, di mattina
Reflexive verbs: mi alzo, mi lavo (first look)
Frequency: sempre, spesso, mai (first look)

kannZiele: You can talk about your hobbies.
You can say what you like and what you don't like.
You can ask others what they do in their free time.
grammatik: piacere: mi piace, mi piacciono
Key irregular verbs: andare, fare, stare, uscire
Modal verbs: voglio, posso (first look)
Linking words: e, o, ma, perché

selbstcheck: I can read and write the letters of the Latin alphabet.
I know a few words in Italian (ciao, grazie, sì, no, buongiorno).
I can say my name in Italian.
I know the numbers from 1 to 10 in Italian (uno … dieci).
I have some time each week to practise at home.
niveaus.selbstcheckNiedrig: No problem: A1.1 is the beginning, you don't need to know anything yet. In the trial lesson we look together at the best way for you to start.

niveaus.label: A1.2
niveaus.ziel: You get by in everyday life: in town, at the doctor, in shops and at the town hall (Comune).

kannZiele: You can ask the way and understand simple directions.
You can buy a ticket for the bus, the metro or the train.
grammatik: Key irregular verbs: andare, venire, uscire
a, in or da: vado a Roma, sono in Italia, vado dal dentista
Saying where: accanto a, davanti a, tra
Question words: Come vado a…? Dov'è…?

kannZiele: You can say what hurts at the doctor's.
You can understand simple advice and instructions.
grammatik: Possessives or article: mi fa male la gamba
Modal verbs: devo, posso, bisogna
wortschatz: At the doctor's (il medico di base, la tessera sanitaria)

bloecke.thema: What are you doing? What will you do?
kannZiele: You can say what you are doing right now.
You can talk about your plans.
You can say what you have done today.
grammatik: stare + gerundio: sto lavorando
Future plans: present, stare per (Domani chiamo il medico)
Passato prossimo with avere: first steps (oggi ho mangiato)

kannZiele: You can say what you do and where you work.
You can describe your working day.
grammatik: essere and stare: sono infermiera, sto cercando lavoro
Article or no article: Sono infermiera. Faccio l'autista.
Key irregular verbs: fare, sapere, dire

kannZiele: You can ask for clothes in a shop and try them on.
You can compare two things.
grammatik: Comparatives: più… di, meno… di
Direct object pronouns: lo, la (Lo ha in blu?)
Demonstratives: questo, quello (quel, quella)
Adjectives: colours and agreement

kannZiele: You can say the date and when something happens.
You can invite someone and accept or say no.
grammatik: Ordinal numbers and dates: primo, secondo; il 3 maggio
Telling the time and days: il lunedì, di sera
Future plans: present for plans (Sabato vado al mare)

kannZiele: You can make an appointment and ask for a form.
You can give your details at a counter (Comune, Poste, ASL).
grammatik: Polite requests: Può…? Vorrei…
Yes/no questions and short answers: Sì, certo. No, non ancora.
Numbers: codice fiscale, phone numbers

selbstcheck: I can introduce myself and ask others their name and where they are from.
I can understand numbers, prices and the time.
I can talk about my family.
I can ask for things in a shop.
I can describe my day with times.

niveaus.label: A2.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about the past, give reasons for your opinion and get by well when you travel.

kannZiele: You can say what your life was like before.
You can talk about what you used to do.
grammatik: Imperfetto: da bambino vivevo, ero, andavo
Frequency: di solito, ogni giorno, a volte
Comparatives: più… di prima

kannZiele: You can say what you did yesterday or last year.
You can tell a short story from your life.
grammatik: Passato prossimo with avere: ho mangiato, ho fatto
Passato prossimo with essere: sono andato/a, sono nato/a
Passato prossimo: già, non ancora, questa settimana

kannZiele: You can describe a flat and say where things are.
You can talk to a neighbour or a landlord about a small problem.
grammatik: Saying where: sopra, sotto, dietro
Prepositions with articles: nel, sul, dal
Indefinites: qualcosa, niente, qualcuno, nessuno

kannZiele: You can explain why you do something.
You can say what you have to do at work.
grammatik: perché, siccome, quindi, allora; penso che
Modal verbs: devo, dobbiamo, bisogna
Indirect object pronouns: gli do, mi pagano

kannZiele: You can say how much you like something.
You can describe how you do things.
grammatik: Quantity: molto, poco, abbastanza, troppo
Adverbs in -mente; bene or buono
piacere: anche a me, neanche a me

kannZiele: You can compare habits and say what is better.
You can talk about your routine and your health.
grammatik: Comparatives and superlatives: (tanto)… quanto, il migliore
Reflexive verbs: mi curo, vado a letto tardi
Negation: non, mai, neanche, niente

kannZiele: You can plan a trip and book a room.
You can pass things on and say who gets what.
grammatik: Future plans: present for trips (Domani parto per Milano)
Indirect object pronouns: gli do, le mando
Direct object pronouns: lo, la, li, le (L'ho prenotato)

selbstcheck: I can say what I have done today (oggi ho…).
I can ask the way and understand the answer.
I can tell a doctor what hurts.
I can make or cancel an appointment.
I can say in a shop what I like and what fits me.

niveaus.label: A2.2
niveaus.ziel: You describe people and things in more detail, give advice and deal with offices and work. A2 is usually the level asked for the long-term EU residence permit; rules change, so check the current requirements before you register for an exam.

kannZiele: You can tell someone about a festival or a party.
You can say when things happened.
grammatik: Passato prossimo: irregular participles (fatto, detto, preso, visto)
Ordinal numbers and dates
Key irregular verbs: review

kannZiele: You can describe what someone is like.
You can say what you have in common.
grammatik: Article or no article: Mi piace il caffè. Ho la macchina.
Adjectives: agreement and position
Comparatives: (tanto)… quanto, tanto quanto

kannZiele: You can ask for help and offer it.
You can give simple advice.
grammatik: Modal verbs: dovere and potere for advice
Polite requests: Le dispiace se…? Potrebbe…?
Reflexive verbs: review (passato prossimo with essere)

kannZiele: You can pay, return a product and complain politely.
You can read a bill and understand the main charges.
grammatik: Direct object pronouns: lo restituisco, la pago
Indefinites: qualche, nessun, altro
Indirect object pronouns: gli mando i documenti

kannZiele: You can talk about the weather and the seasons in Italy.
You can say what you do for the environment.
grammatik: Quantity: molto, troppo, tanto: review
Imperfetto: describing the weather and the place
Negation: nessuno, niente, double negation

kannZiele: You can talk about your work experience.
You can answer simple questions in an interview.
grammatik: Passato prossimo and imperfetto in your CV
perché, siccome, quindi
Frequency: sempre, spesso, di solito

kannZiele: You can explain what you need at an office (permesso di soggiorno, codice fiscale, tessera sanitaria) and understand what to bring.
You can ask someone to repeat or to write something down.
grammatik: Polite requests: Potrebbe…? Vorrei…
Direct object pronouns: Lo porto? La firmo?
Ordinal numbers: il primo piano, il secondo sportello

selbstcheck: I can talk about my childhood.
I can give reasons with perché and siccome.
I can ask politely: Può…? Vorrei…
I can compare things: più grande di, il migliore.
I can talk about my hobbies (mi interessa, mi piace).

niveaus.label: B1.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about experiences, plans and opinions, also on topics that are less familiar.

kannZiele: You can tell the story of your life or of a journey in the right order.
You can describe the background of an event.
grammatik: Passato prossimo or imperfetto: telling a story
Trapassato prossimo: avevo già mangiato
Time: da, per, fa, fra, durante

kannZiele: You can talk about your experience and your plans at work.
You can write a short email to a company.
grammatik: Verbal periphrases: stare per, finire di, smettere di, continuare a
Relative clauses: che, cui, quello che

kannZiele: You can say what you think about the news and social media.
You can give arguments for and against.
grammatik: Linkers: anche se, però, tuttavia, inoltre
Verbs + prepositions: pensare a, dipendere da

kannZiele: You can follow a doctor's instructions and ask for details.
You can tell someone what to do and what not to do.
grammatik: Imperative: prendi, non prendere, prendilo
Verbs like piacere: servire, mancare, bastare
wortschatz: The health system (SSN, medico di base)

kannZiele: You can sort out a problem with a landlord or flatmates.
You can say what would be better.
grammatik: Real conditions: se + present
Condizionale presente: vorrei, io al tuo posto
Stressed pronouns: a me, per te, con lui

kannZiele: You can talk about plans and predictions.
You can solve a problem while travelling.
grammatik: Futuro semplice: parlerò, avrò
ci and ne: ci vuole un'ora, ne ho due

kannZiele: You can talk about relationships and what people are like.
You can pass something on and say who gets what.
grammatik: sapere or conoscere; portare or prendere
Combined pronouns: me lo, te la, glielo

selbstcheck: I can talk about past events with the passato prossimo and the imperfetto.
I can give advice: Devi… Dovresti…
I can describe people and things with essere, stare and adjectives.
I can write a simple email to a company.
I can say when something happened with quando and dopo.

niveaus.label: B1.2
niveaus.ziel: You discuss, describe processes and write clear texts, and you are ready for a B1 exam. B1 is usually the level asked as language proof for Italian citizenship; the rules changed recently, so check the current requirements before you apply.

kannZiele: You can say what you hope and what you want others to do.
You can discuss what should change.
grammatik: Congiuntivo presente: the forms (parli, abbia, vada)
Congiuntivo after wishes and feelings: spero che, voglio che

kannZiele: You can talk about courses and qualifications.
You can say what something is for.
grammatik: Infinitive or congiuntivo: voglio andare, voglio che tu vada
Purpose: per + infinitive, affinché + congiuntivo

kannZiele: You can report what other people say.
You can ask for information politely.
grammatik: Indirect questions and reporting: dice che, mi chiede se, non so dove
Relative clauses: quello che, in cui

kannZiele: You can compare offers and make a complaint.
You can talk about what is on sale and what is closed.
grammatik: Participles: il negozio è chiuso, aperto
Adjective position and short forms: un buon prezzo, un bel regalo
Word formation: -zione, -tà, -mento, -ista

kannZiele: You can talk about what will happen when things change.
You can write a formal email or a complaint.
grammatik: Time clauses: quando arrivo, appena, finché
il + adjective: l'importante è, quello che

kannZiele: You can talk about films, books and events.
You can recommend something and say why.
grammatik: Verbs + prepositions: sognare di, ricordarsi di, abituarsi a
Verbs like piacere: interessare, sembrare, dispiacere

kannZiele: You know the format of the exam you want to take and can manage your time.
You can do a full practice test.
grammatik: Review: past tenses and time clauses
Review: congiuntivo and conditions
wortschatz: Useful phrases for writing and speaking

selbstcheck: I can tell a story in the right order (prima, poi, mentre).
I can give my opinion and support it with anche se and tuttavia.
I can say what I would like to do (mi piacerebbe…).
I can write a complaint or a formal email.
I can plan a meeting or a trip with other people.

niveaus.label: B2.1
niveaus.ziel: You understand longer texts, argue convincingly and write in a formal style, at work and in study.

kannZiele: You can discuss working conditions and give reasons for your view.
You can write a formal letter of application.
grammatik: Congiuntivo in opinion and doubt: credo che, può darsi che
Collocations: prendere una decisione, fare un giro

kannZiele: You can follow a news report and say what it means.
You can report what was said.
grammatik: Passive and si: si dice, si affitta, è stato approvato
Reported speech with tense shifts: ha detto che sarebbe venuto

kannZiele: You can describe the housing market where you live.
You can say exactly what you are looking for.
grammatik: Relative clauses with congiuntivo and prepositions: cerco un appartamento che abbia…
Concession and consequence: benché + congiuntivo

kannZiele: You can talk about stress, moods and how people change.
You can tell someone about a small accident or a mistake.
grammatik: Verbs of change: diventare, farsi, rimanere
Gerundio and participle constructions: avendo finito, essendo stanco

kannZiele: You can talk about what would be different under other conditions.
You can say what you wanted other people to do.
grammatik: Congiuntivo imperfetto: volevo che venissi
Periodo ipotetico: se avessi, comprerei

kannZiele: You can read a contract or terms and ask about the details.
You can explain results and effects.
grammatik: Adjectives + prepositions: stufo di, capace di, interessato a
Concession and consequence: così… che, in modo che

kannZiele: You can keep a conversation going and interrupt politely.
You can guess what has happened and say how sure you are.
grammatik: Discourse markers in speech: allora, cioè, insomma, boh
Probability: saranno le tre, sarà uscito

selbstcheck: I have finished B1 or feel confident at B1.
I can use the congiuntivo presente for wishes and feelings.
I can link ideas with anche se, tuttavia and quindi.
I can give a talk on a topic for 3–4 minutes.
I understand the main points of the news on the radio.

niveaus.label: B2.2
niveaus.ziel: You write and speak precisely, also about abstract topics, and you are ready for a B2 exam.

kannZiele: You can discuss scenarios and what could happen.
You can weigh up possible solutions.
grammatik: Probability: futuro and condizionale of conjecture
Periodo ipotetico: se avessi saputo, sarei venuto (introduction)

kannZiele: You can summarise a report in your own words.
You can describe processes in a formal style.
grammatik: Passive and si: si è dimostrato, è stato scoperto
Nominalisation in formal writing (introduction)

kannZiele: You can explain how decisions are made in Italy.
You can report requests and demands.
grammatik: Reported speech with tense shifts: mi ha chiesto di aiutarlo
Congiuntivo in opinion and doubt: dubito che, non è vero che

kannZiele: You can talk about belonging, languages and customs.
You can describe how a person or a place has changed.
grammatik: Relative clauses with congiuntivo and prepositions: la casa in cui abito, il quale
Verbs of change: diventare, farsi, rimanere

kannZiele: You can write a report or a review.
You can say what you would like to happen.
grammatik: Congiuntivo imperfetto: vorrei che, magari potessi
Collocations: dare una mano, presentare reclamo, avere voglia di

kannZiele: You can discuss a rule or a law and say what you think of it.
You can make a formal complaint.
grammatik: Concession and consequence: per quanto, benché
Adjectives + prepositions: contento di, responsabile di

kannZiele: You know the format of the exam you want to take and can manage your time.
You can do a full practice test.
grammatik: Review: congiuntivo and conditions
Review: reported speech and linkers
wortschatz: Useful phrases for writing and speaking

selbstcheck: I can write formal emails without help.
I understand the congiuntivo imperfetto when I read it.
I can report what someone said (ha detto che…).
I can disagree in a discussion and suggest a compromise.
I understand newspaper articles on familiar topics.

niveaus.label: C1
niveaus.ziel: You understand demanding texts, speak spontaneously and fluently, and write well-structured texts.

kannZiele: You can understand long factual texts and summarise them.
You can present results in a formal style.
grammatik: Nominalisation in formal writing
Sequence of tenses: congiuntivo trapassato

kannZiele: You can write a report or a proposal.
You can lead a meeting and sum up.
grammatik: Non-finite clauses: finita la riunione, dopo aver finito
Formal connectors: a causa di, pertanto, ai sensi di

kannZiele: You can argue about abstract topics and answer counter-arguments.
You can set conditions and limits precisely.
grammatik: Conditions without se: purché, a meno che non, qualora
Formal relatives: il quale, la cui

kannZiele: You can tell fact from opinion in a long article or a programme.
You can put the focus exactly where you want it.
grammatik: Emphasis and cleft sentences: È Anna che…, Quello che mi serve è…
Passato remoto: andai, fu, disse (in texts and in southern speech)

kannZiele: You can talk about how language varies in Italy and the Italian-speaking world.
You can switch between formal and informal style.
grammatik: Prefixes and derivation: dis-, ri-, pre-, in-, sovra-
Discourse markers and register

kannZiele: You can explain complex causes and effects.
You can turn a spoken explanation into formal writing.
grammatik: Nominalisation and verbal style: decidere, la decisione
Formal connectors: tuttavia, pertanto, nondimeno

kannZiele: You can write a review and give a nuanced opinion.
You can follow a discussion about a film or a book.
grammatik: come se + congiuntivo; Se l'avessi saputo, sarei venuto
Cohesion: reference, ellipsis, ciò, quello

kannZiele: You know the format of the exam you want to take and can manage your time.
You can do a full practice test.
grammatik: Review: formal style and sentence structure
Review: congiuntivo and sequence of tenses
wortschatz: Useful phrases for writing and speaking

selbstcheck: I have finished B2 or feel confident at B2.
I can report what other people said, with the right tenses.
I can argue about abstract topics and give counter-arguments.
I understand factual texts and talks on most topics.
I can switch between a formal and an informal style.
